Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
options(scipen = 999)

Data

For this homework, we are going to use the Gapminder data on population (pop), GDP per capita (gdp), and life expectancy (lex). These data were downloaded and compiled using the gapminder_compile.Rmd script in the data folder.

Let’s focus our attention on data from the past 100 years, between 1925 and 2025.

gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1925, 2025))
  1. Use the function(s) of your choice to get an idea of the overall structure of the data, including its dimensions, column names, classes, etc.
glimpse(gapminder)

  1. How many countries are represented in this dataset?
gapminder %>% 
  summarize(n_country = n_distinct(country))
## # A tibble: 1 × 1
##   n_country
##       <int>
## 1       195
  1. Which five countries have had the largest absolute population growth between 1925-2025? Show this as a table.
gapminder_pop_growth <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 1925 | year == 2025) %>% 
  select(country, year, pop) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, 
              values_from = pop, 
              names_prefix = "pop_") %>% 
  mutate(pop_growth = pop_2025 - pop_1925) 

gapminder_pop_growth %>% 
  arrange(desc(pop_growth)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    pop_1925   pop_2025 pop_growth
##   <chr>         <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 India     304406019 1463865525 1159459506
## 2 China     473741473 1416096094  942354621
## 3 Indonesia  49685263  285721236  236035973
## 4 Pakistan   22624808  255219554  232594746
## 5 USA       116193761  347275807  231082046
  1. Make a plot that shows population growth over time for the top country you found in question #3.
# Top country found in Question #3 was India. 
gapminder %>% 
  filter(country == "India") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = pop)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Population Growth Over Time (India)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Population")

  1. Has global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025? Show the min, median, mean, and max for all countries (combined) in the dataset.
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 1925) %>% 
  drop_na(lex) %>% 
  summarize(lex_min = min(lex),
         lex_med = median(lex),
         lex_mean = mean(lex),
         lex_max = max(lex))
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   lex_min lex_med lex_mean lex_max
##     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1    21.0    35.9     38.1    63.5
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 2025) %>% 
  drop_na(lex) %>% 
  summarize(lex_min = min(lex),
         lex_med = median(lex),
         lex_mean = mean(lex),
         lex_max = max(lex))
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   lex_min lex_med lex_mean lex_max
##     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1    52.8    74.8     73.9    85.6

Differences across all of these measures indicates that global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025.

  1. Make a plot that shows the distribution of life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025 (try using geom_density). What do you notice about the shift in life expectancy over time?
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 1925 | year == 2025) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.factor(year)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = lex, fill = year)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Life Expectancy in All Countries in 1925 and 2025",
       x = "Life Expectancy (Years)",
       y = "Density") 
## Warning: Removed 13 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_density()`).

The life expectancy greatly shifted over to the left over time, indicating that the life expectancy increased over time (people in 2025 are expected to have longer lifespans than people in 1925).

  1. We are interested in the relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy; i.e. does having more money help you live longer in 2025? Show this as a plot. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 2025, country != "Monaco") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp, y = lex)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "GDP per Capita vs. Life Expectancy (2025)",
       x = "GDP per Capita",
       y = "Life Expectancy") 
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Which five countries have had the highest absolute GDP per capita growth over the past 50 years? Show this as a table. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gapminder_gdp_growth <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 1975 | year == 2025, country != "Monaco") %>% #past 50 years = 1975-2025
  select(country, year, gdp) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = gdp, 
              names_prefix = "gdp_") %>% 
  mutate(gdp_growth = gdp_2025 - gdp_1975)  

gapminder_gdp_growth %>% 
  arrange(desc(gdp_growth)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    gdp_1975 gdp_2025 gdp_growth
##   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 Singapore    12896.  137906.    125010.
## 2 Ireland      14336.  119406.    105071.
## 3 Luxembourg   30950.  131038.    100088.
## 4 Guyana        5071.   79371.     74300.
## 5 Norway       25513.   94896.     69382.
  1. How does per capita GDP growth compare between these same five countries over the past 50 years? Show this as a plot.
# Top 5 Countries: Singapore, Ireland, Luxembourg, Guyana, Norway  
gapminder %>% 
  filter((country == "Singapore" |
         country == "Ireland" |
         country == "Luxembourg" |
         country == "Guyana" |
         country == "Norway"),
         year >= 1975) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = gdp, color = country)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "GDP per Capita Growth (1975-2025)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "GDP per Capita")

  1. Do one analysis of your choice that includes a table and plot as outputs.
# Analysis will be what were the top five countries with the highest increase in life expectancy in the past 50 years and what was the trend for each country's life expectancy across the past 50 years. 
gapminder_lex_growth <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year == 1975 | year == 2025) %>% 
  select(country, year, lex) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = lex, 
              names_prefix = "lex_") %>% 
  mutate(lex_growth = lex_2025 - lex_1975)  

gapminder_lex_growth %>% 
  arrange(desc(lex_growth)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    lex_1975 lex_2025 lex_growth
##   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 Cambodia       24.7     71.0       46.4
## 2 Maldives       51.7     80.5       28.8
## 3 Ethiopia       43.2     70.7       27.5
## 4 Bangladesh     50.6     76.3       25.7
## 5 Lao            45.5     70.6       25.1
# Top 5 Countries: Cambodia, Maldives, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, Lao  
gapminder %>% 
  filter((country == "Cambodia" |
         country == "Maldives" |
         country == "Ethiopia" |
         country == "Bangladesh" |
         country == "Lao"),
         year >= 1975) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = lex, color = country)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Life Expectancy Across 1975 to 2025",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Life Expectancy (Years)")
